question: You see an endpoint that loads 50 orders then runs a query per order for line items. How do you detect and fix this N+1 pattern?
shortAnswer: Detect via query logs/APM, then fetch children in one query (JOIN or WHERE IN / JOIN FETCH) and assemble in memory.
strongAnswer: Confirm with DB logs or an APM showing 1+N queries. Replace with a single JOIN or two-query approach: select orders, then select items where order_id IN (...), group in the app. Add indexes supporting the lookup. Prefer explicit queries over accidental ORM lazy loads in hot paths.
advancedAnswer: Discuss dataloader patterns, pagination interaction, and when denormalized read models help.
followUps: How do ORMs cause accidental N+1?
commonWrongAnswer: Cache each per-order query in Redis without reducing query count at the source.
codeExample:
-- better: one query for items
SELECT * FROM order_items WHERE order_id = ANY($1::uuid[]);
productionRelevance: N+1 silently kills latency as datasets grow—common interview and production topic.
